title: The Heart Nutrient You Might Be Missing
hook: Hitting your five-a-day may not be enough: researchers say foods rich in flavanols — berries, apples, beans, tea — are a separate lever for heart health most diets miss.
key_points: Flavanols are plant compounds linked to better heart health, distinct from just eating more produce.
Five servings of fruit and veg a day can still fall short on flavanols.
Blackberries, plums, apples, broad beans, cherries, and green tea are standout sources.
Choosing flavanol-rich options can sharply raise intake without eating more overall.
content_html: "Eat your five a day" is good advice, but a study summarized by ScienceDaily suggests it can miss something specific: flavanols, a family of plant compounds tied to better heart health. Hit your produce quota with the wrong foods and you can still come up short.
extra_html:
Flavanols occur in some plant foods far more than others, so the kind of fruit and vegetable you reach for changes how much you get. Researchers point to standout sources — blackberries, plums, apples, broad beans, cherries, and green tea — and note that leaning toward these can dramatically increase flavanol intake without eating any more food overall.

The takeaway isn't to chase a single super-nutrient or buy supplements; it's a small tilt in everyday choices. Swapping in a handful of berries, an apple, or a cup of green tea is an easy way to fold more flavanols into a diet that's already aiming for variety — and a reminder that with produce, what you pick matters as much as how much.

related.title: Building a Balanced Plate
related.hook: Forget counting every calorie — the simplest healthy-eating tool is a picture of a plate: half produce, a quarter grains, a quarter protein.

related.title: Tea Is Good for You — Until You Add the Wrong Things
related.hook: A major review ties tea to lower risks of heart disease, diabetes, cancer, and cognitive decline — but warns that bottled and bubble teas often pack in ingredients that cancel out the benefits.

related.title: Keeping Your Heart Healthy
related.hook: Most heart disease isn't bad luck — it's the sum of a few everyday habits. The American Heart Association distills them into eight that move the needle most.

flashcards.prompt: Why might eating five servings of fruit and veg a day still leave a gap for heart health?
flashcards.back_html: Because not all produce is rich in flavanols — the heart-linked compounds. Which fruits and vegetables you choose matters, not just how many.

flashcards.prompt: Which of these was highlighted as a strong source of flavanols?
flashcards.explanation_html: Researchers pointed to blackberries, plums, apples, broad beans, cherries, and green tea as choices that can dramatically increase flavanol intake.
